title: Reasons 4-6: infinity; consensus of the wise; pagan deities as names of one
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): YE FOURTH: either God is one, or if many, infinitely many must be — but infinitely many cannot be. YE FIFTH from ye unanimous consensus belonging toward all ye wise. YE SIXTH: most names belonging toward ye Gentiles' gods designate one God under diverse attributes — Jupiter plus Pluto, Phoebus, Dionysus are one. God stands as one in all. Though God is one, by many names He is called.
pass_b_english: THE FOURTH: either God is one, or if there are many there must be infinitely many; but there cannot be infinitely many.
THE FIFTH is from the unanimous consensus of all the wise.

THE SIXTH: most names of the Gentiles' gods designate one God under diverse attributes. Jupiter and Pluto, Phoebus, Dionysus are one. God stands as one in all. The philosopher On the World to Alexander: though God is one, He is called by many names.
source_text: QUARTA: aut unus est Deus, aut si plures sint infinitos esse oportet; infiniti autem esse nequeunt. QUINTA est a sapientum omnium unanimi consensu. SEXTA: plurima gentilitiorum deorum nomina unum Deum designant diversis attributis. Jupiter & Pluto, Phoebus, Dionysus unum est. Deus assistat in omnibus unus. Philosophus de mundo ad Alexandrum: Unus Deus cum sit, pluribus nominibus est appellatus.
